data: Are the blue circles (representing 19th century poems) generally positioned to the left of the blue triangles (representing Imagist poems) in the plot?

The scatter plot shows three different groups of data points: 19th century poems represented by blue circles, Imagist poems represented by blue triangles, and contemporary poems represented by dark blue dots. The x-axis represents the publication year, and the y-axis represents the arousal score.

To determine if the blue circles (representing 19th century poems) are generally positioned to the left of the blue triangles (representing Imagist poems), we need to compare their positions along the x-axis.

From the figure, it is clear that the 19th century poems (blue circles) are generally positioned to the left of the Imagist poems (blue triangles). This can be observed by noting that the majority of the blue circles are located before the blue triangles on the x-axis.

Therefore, the answer is yes, the blue circles are generally positioned to the left of the blue triangles in the plot.
